Accountable obligation owner.value: Filing determination owner; escalation to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — each state's rate/form filing statute plus that state's SERFF General Instructions and Product Requirements Locator entry, re-read at determination time (rep: Oklahoma Title 36)

In-scope processes.value: Product development change intake → filing determination gate, for every form, rate, rule and manual change across the 50 SERFF jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: SERFF Filing Rules + Filing Access; determinations logged in the filing tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Filing Determination Procedure (pre-use gate) — intake, classification, per-state review-method lookup, exemption basis, deemer math, log entry

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by Chief Compliance Officer; reviewed annually and on any state filing-rule bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per filing — determination must close before the product build freeze; prior-approval states drive the latest-submission date backed off the target effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker milestone alerts at T-90/T-60/T-30 days to target effective date for every open determination

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Determination worksheet, dated state filing-rules captures and counsel sign-off retained 7 years from form/rate withdrawal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any change implemented without a determination is logged as a compliance exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every 'no filing required' call and every late/unfiled remediation

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All product/form/rate/rule changes implemented in the quarter per the policy admin change log, across all writing companies and states

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any implemented change with no determination on file before its effective date is a fail; ≥1 fail escalates to the CCO

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per-filing; test runs quarterly over that quarter's population plus 100% review of prior-approval states

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored any sampled determination

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly filing-determination test workpaper (population extract, sample, re-performance notes, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Determination log export + SERFF tracking numbers + approval letters, presentable as a market conduct exam response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct Compliance owns the exam/inquiry response; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of an unfiled change before it is sent

checklist.step: Take in the approved product change and open a determination worksheet
actions: Open the product change queue and filter Status = 'Approved for filing determination'.
Copy onto a new determination worksheet: product name, writing company and NAIC co-code, TOI/Sub-TOI, target effective date, affected states, new-business-only vs new + in-force.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the business driver and the hard date driver (competitor response, statutory mandate, release train) and record it.
Attach the signed change request to the determination folder named <company>-<TOI>-<effective date>.
checklist.done: the worksheet carries product, company, TOI/Sub-TOI, target date and state list, with the change request attached.

checklist.step: Break the change into filable elements and tag each one
actions: List every artifact the change touches on its own worksheet row.

Tag each row FORM (policy form, endorsement, application, rider, notice), RATE (base rates, factors, tiers, territory relativities), RULE (eligibility/underwriting rule, manual page) or NON-FILED (marketing collateral, internal procedure).
For FORM rows copy the form number and edition date exactly as printed in the form footer.
For RATE rows get the statewide rate level impact % per state from Pricing and paste it on the row.
Email the Pricing Actuary to confirm the rate level impact figures in writing; file the reply.
checklist.done: every touched artifact has a row, a tag, and (for rate rows) a written rate level impact % from Pricing.

checklist.step: Collect the filing-grade source artifacts from Product Development and Pricing
actions: Request from Product Development: print-ready form PDFs with form number and edition date on every page, plus a redline against the currently approved edition.
Request from Pricing: rate exhibits, rating manual pages and the draft actuarial memorandum with the certification page.
Open every PDF and check it is text-searchable, watermark-free, and under the SERFF attachment size cap (3 MB per attachment as a rule of thumb).
Reject and re-request anything marked DRAFT or missing an edition date rather than filing around it.
Save the accepted set into the determination folder.
checklist.done: the artifact set is complete, watermark-free, and the redline scope matches the change request scope.

checklist.step: Read each affected state's current SERFF filing rules for this TOI
actions: Log in to SERFF (login.serff.com) with the company instance and your industry user id.
From the Industry menu open 'Filing Rules', or open the state's entry in the NAIC Product Requirements Locator.
Select the state, then the Business Type and the TOI/Sub-TOI matching the change.
Read the state's General Instructions and open any attached filing-requirements checklist or state-specific transmittal.
Print the instructions page to PDF, name it <state>-filing-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it — this is the evidence behind the review-method call.
Repeat for every affected state and note any bulletins the instructions reference.
checklist.done: a dated filing-rules capture exists in the folder for every affected state.

checklist.step: Record the review method per state per element
actions: On each worksheet row, set the review method: PRIOR APPROVAL, FILE-AND-USE, USE-AND-FILE, INFORMATIONAL/FILE-FOR-RECORD or EXEMPT.
Paste the exact sentence from the state instructions plus the statutory or bulletin cite you relied on into the row.
Where the instructions are silent or ambiguous, email the state's SERFF contact from the state's SERFF page and log the question, date and answer on the row.
Highlight every PRIOR APPROVAL state — those set the critical path.
checklist.done: every state/element row has a review method, a quoted source sentence and a citation.

checklist.step: Confirm the product coding and the submission channel each state accepts
actions: Open the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix for the line and locate the TOI and Sub-TOI that match the product.
Check the state's SERFF Filing Rules page lists that TOI as accepted through SERFF.
Where the state takes the line outside SERFF, record the alternate channel (state portal URL or paper filing address) and its own instructions.
Write TOI, Sub-TOI and submission channel onto every state row.
checklist.done: TOI, Sub-TOI and submission channel are recorded and agree with the coding matrix for every state.

checklist.step: Support every 'no filing required' call with a named exemption
actions: For each EXEMPT/NON-FILED row, name the basis: commercial large-risk or exempt commercial purchaser exemption, surplus lines, non-filed inland marine class, informational-only material, or out-of-scope internal procedure.
Paste the statute, regulation or bulletin cite that grants the exemption, with its effective date.
Where the exemption depends on a threshold (premium size, insured net worth), record the tested value and where it came from.
Never leave a row reading only 'not required'.
checklist.done: every exempt row carries a named exemption, a citation and (where thresholds apply) the tested value.

checklist.step: Search SERFF Filing Access for an existing approval that already covers the change
actions: In SERFF open Filing Access and search by company (or NAIC co-code), state, TOI and form number.
Filter Disposition to Approved / Filed / Closed-Approved and sort by disposition date descending.
Open the closest match and compare the approved form edition and rate exhibit to the new edition.
Decide reuse vs new filing: reuse only where the approved text and rates are unchanged for that state.
Copy the SERFF Tracking Number and disposition date onto the worksheet row when reuse applies.
checklist.done: each row states reuse (with SERFF tracking number) or new filing, based on an inspected prior filing.

checklist.step: Compute the deemer clock and the latest submission date per state
actions: Read the review period / deemer days from the state instructions or statute (commonly 30, 45 or 60 days) and record it on the row.
Add the internal lead times: package preparation days, actuarial review days, and an objection-response buffer (10 business days is the working assumption).
Compute latest submission date = target effective date − (deemer days + objection buffer + implementation lead) and write it on the row.
Load each latest submission date into the filing calendar and set T-90/T-60/T-30 reminders against the target effective date.
checklist.done: every state row shows deemer days, the computed latest submission date, and a calendar entry with reminders.

checklist.step: Fix the package scope by listing what each state will demand with the filing
actions: From each state's filing-requirements checklist, list the companion items: actuarial memorandum and certification, rate/rule schedule, Statement of Variability, readability (Flesch) certification, side-by-side redline, cover letter, third-party filer authorization, filing fee amount and payment method (EFT vs check).
Name the owner and due date for each companion item and hand them to Pricing, Product Development or Legal as applicable.
Flag any item with a long lead time (Flesch scoring, translated forms, third-party authorization) so it starts now.
checklist.done: each state has a companion-item list with an owner and a due date ahead of the latest submission date.

checklist.step: Write the determination row into the Filing Determination Log
actions: For every state and element, add a log row: change id, state, element, filing required Y/N, review method, filing type, statutory cite, deemer days, latest submission date, reuse tracking number, decider and decision date.
Link the log row to the determination folder holding the dated filing-rules captures.
Set the log row status to 'Determined — pending counsel' where sign-off is required, otherwise 'Determined — closed'.
checklist.done: the log holds one complete, source-linked row per state per element with no blank fields.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel sign-off on the risky calls before closing the log rows
actions: Route to counsel every 'no filing required' determination and every prior-approval state row.
Counsel re-reads the cited statute/bulletin and either confirms or overturns the call in writing on the row.
Overturned rows go back to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for rework the same week.
Confirmed rows get counsel name and date stamped, then move to 'Determined — closed'.
checklist.done: no exempt or prior-approval row is closed without a dated counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Publish the determination back to the product change record and arm the go-live gate
actions: Attach the determination summary to the product change record.
Set the release gate flag on every prior-approval state: no rate, form or rule may be used in that state until an approval or a satisfied deemer is recorded.
Give the implementation team the per-state earliest-use dates so the policy admin and rating configuration is dated accordingly.
Add the filing milestones to the product release plan.
checklist.done: the change record shows a per-state earliest-use date and prior-approval states are blocked in the release plan.

checklist.step: Escalate when the target effective date cannot survive the state's review timeline
actions: Compare the latest submission date to today plus the package-prep estimate for every state.
Where the date is already unreachable, raise an escalation to the Chief Compliance Officer and the product sponsor within one business day.
Present the options in writing: move the effective date, drop the state from the launch, or launch on the previously approved forms/rates.
Record the decision and its owner on the determination log row — skipping the filing is never one of the options.
checklist.done: every unreachable date has a written, owned decision that keeps the state either compliant or out of the launch.

checklist.step: Retain the determination evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the determination folder (worksheet, dated filing-rules captures, counsel sign-offs, rate impact confirmations) into the compliance evidence repository under the product and effective date.
Apply the 7-year-from-withdrawal retention label so the record survives product sunset.
Confirm the repository index shows the record as searchable by state, form number and SERFF tracking number.
checklist.done: the determination record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by state and form number.

testing.step: Build the population of changes that actually went live in the quarter
actions: Extract from the policy administration change log every form, rate, rule and manual change with an effective date inside the quarter, by writing company and state.
Add rating-engine configuration releases and manual-page publications so system-only changes cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract count to the release notes for the quarter and resolve any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to release records and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every implemented change to a determination that pre-dates it
actions: Match each population row to a Filing Determination Log row on change id + state + element.
Check the determination decision date is earlier than the change's effective date.
List unmatched rows and late determinations as automatic exceptions — no judgement, no exceptions to the exception.
testing.done: every population row is matched to a pre-dated determination or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of rows in prior-approval states.
Take 25 rows selected at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining population, minimum 40 rows in total.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every prior-approval state row.

testing.step: Re-perform the review-method call in SERFF for each sampled row
actions: Open SERFF Filing Rules (or the Product Requirements Locator) for the sampled state and TOI as of the determination date.
Read the General Instructions and reach your own review-method conclusion without looking at the worksheet first.
Compare to the recorded determination; any difference is an exception, including 'right answer, wrong citation'.
Screenshot the instructions page you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent re-performance note and a captured source page.

testing.step: Check the product coding and submission channel on the sample
actions: Look up the product in the NAIC Uniform Product Coding Matrix and compare the TOI/Sub-TOI to the determination row.
Confirm the recorded submission channel matches what the state's SERFF page accepts for that TOI.
Flag miscoded rows — a wrong TOI usually means the wrong instructions were read.
testing.done: TOI, Sub-TOI and channel agree with the coding matrix for every sampled row, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Test the support behind every 'no filing required' call in the sample
actions: Pull each exempt row and read the cited statute, regulation or bulletin as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the exemption actually covers the element filed under it, including any premium or net-worth threshold and the tested value.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off exists and pre-dates the go-live date.
Treat a generic 'not required' with no cite as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every exempt row is supported by a verified citation, tested threshold and dated counsel sign-off.

testing.step: Trace every 'filing required' row to a SERFF submission that pre-dates go-live
actions: In SERFF Filing Access, search the recorded SERFF Tracking Number for the sampled row.
Confirm the filing exists for the right company, state, TOI and form number/edition.
Read the submission date and the disposition (Filed / Approved / Closed) and compare both to the change's effective date.
Where reuse of a prior approval was claimed, open that prior filing and confirm the approved edition is genuinely the one in use.
Capture the SERFF filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every filing-required row traces to a real SERFF filing submitted before the change went live.

testing.step: Recompute the deemer maths and prove the release gate held
actions: For 10 sampled prior-approval rows, recompute latest submission date = effective date − (deemer days + objection buffer + implementation lead).
Compare the actual submission date to the recomputed date and note any filing submitted late.
Check the policy admin/rating effective date is on or after the approval date or the satisfied deemer date.
Any use before approval or before a satisfied deemer is a reportable compliance breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled state was used before approval or a satisfied deemer, and deemer maths reconciles.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the change id, state, what was missed and the compliance impact.
Assign a root cause (intake missed the change, wrong TOI, stale instructions, timeline crushed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for use-before-approval breaches, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-unfiled-change threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the evidence references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer — who authored none of the sampled determinations — sign the workpaper.
Report results and open breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.
